newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says aluminium plant to open in few months.
newsitem.headline: Iran says aluminium plant to open in few months.

text.p: The first unit of a new aluminium smelter in Iran will come onstream in a few months, two years behind schedule, an official said in remarks published on Wednesday.

Deputy Minister of Mines and Metals Ali Golestaneh, quoted by the daily Abrar, said the 30,000-tonne unit of the Al-Mahdi smelter near the Gulf port of Bandar Abbas would open in the early part of the new Iranian year that starts on March 21.

Golestaneh said production at the plant, being built at a cost of more than $1.25 billion, would gradually increase to an annual 110,000 tonnes in the first phase of the project and eventually to 330,000 tonnes. He did not give a timetable.

Iran had said the first phase of the smelter would be completed in early 1995. The report gave no reason for the delay and officials were not available for comment. Some experts have blamed lack of funds for the construction delays.
Tehran said in December the water desalination unit of the smelter had started operating.
The country's ageing smelter at Arak produced 117,000 tonnes in the Iranian year that ended in March 1996, officials said.
